source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Data Canopy's Lithia Springs campus is a documented 10 MW of IT load, which is mid-scale for AI compute, not hyperscale.

The operator publishes 10 MW of IT capacity and 19,500 square feet of technical space, and nothing else that would settle density. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 10 MW is roughly 250 racks. At 10 kW per rack it is about 1,000 racks. The published square footage favors the lower rack count, because 250 racks across 19,500 square feet implies about 78 square feet per rack, while 1,000 racks would imply under 20 square feet per rack, which is tight for training gear. Any rack conversion is an inference, not an operator figure.

The only published certification is LEED. That is a green building rating and says nothing about power redundancy, cooling topology, or network paths. It does not establish whether the campus can host high-density training racks.

Georgia has 49 mapped facilities, and only five publish a megawatt figure. Those five total 76.3 MW, so this campus is about 13 percent of the state's published capacity and ranks third in the state. Most Georgia facilities publish no figure, so the published total is a floor. The data covers one operator's published capacity and the state's sparse published totals. It does not cover actual grid load, interconnection status, or power procurement, which is where the constraint on AI scaling sits.
